chapter: Boston, Buffalo and finding a style
title: Passing tones and the pop tunes that opened up the harmony
summary: Half his work was bowed solos and humming; passing tones replaced plain triads, helped by ballads like The Man I Love and Tenderly.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Now, when you were, now, what kind of things were you guys working on in those periods, at that point in the '30s?

Well, it was -- of course, myself, I was doing more -- at least half of my work was solo, soloing, you know, bowing, my humming, you know, but basically it's like boo-pa-doo-dum, you know, skipping and what have you?
What have you, passing tones. Passing tones, what would you say, elaborate upon more passing tones instead of straight triads and what have you.
Uh-huh. So passing tones were starting to come into it. Now, was that, did that come about from bass players, from the guys getting bored with the triadic harmonies,
or certain kinds of tunes that you were playing start to lead you into those kind of things?
Well, could be, been getting bored from the triads and what have you, and, of course, certain kinds of tunes that we played called for passing tones and what have you.
Do you remember any of the tunes that -- any tunes stick out in your mind from that period the guys were kind of fascinated with that gave them some other directions harmonically?
Well, It's hard to -- that was around '35.
Yeah, right around that period those, you started to come in.
Oh, gees, a lot of tunes, if I could get in my little dictionary and what have you, I could remember some of those great tunes, pop tunes, ballads like, slower numbers.
You mean like tunes like maybe like 'The Man I Love' and stuff, some of those kind of tunes?

Yeah, because that takes you through some stuff. Yeah, some of those tunes would take you like -- yeah, because that was one of the things, one guy said he felt that the music, that was when the music began to evolve a
certain way was when guys started playing, when the repertoire moved into other areas beside the blues.
How about 'Tenderly' and tunes like that? They were coming along then?
And the guys, yeah. So now, when you -- let me turn this off for a second.
